name: Smoked Haddock with Charred Courgette & Crispy New Potatoes
why: The classic haddock, courgette and potato trio done properly: dry-chared courgette for a smoky echo of the fish, properly crispy roasted potatoes, and a lemon lemongrass butter sauce with a secret splash of fish sauce for umami depth.
author: Henry
ingredients: 2 fresh smoked haddock fillets (~400g), skin on
1 lemongrass stalk (or 1 tsp grated fresh ginger as fallback)
Pinch of chilli flakes (or pinch of crushed dried chilli)
Bay leaf, olive oil, fresh thyme or dill, salt

steps: Bring a large pan of well-salted water to a boil for the potatoes.
Shred the lemongrass (chop off the woody end, slice thin, then mince) and grate the garlic.
Zest and juice the lemon. Chop herbs.
Parboil the new potatoes for 5 minutes — just firm at the centre. Drain and shake the pan to rough up the edges (this is what makes them crispy).
Toss with olive oil, pile on a tray, and roast at 220°C for 25–30 min until deeply golden and crisp. Turn once.

While the potatoes roast: place the haddock skin-side down in a wide pan with the white wine, a splash of water, the lemon and the bay leaf. Bring to a bare simmer, cover and cook for 8 minutes. It's done when it flakes easily — don't overcook.
Heat a dry pan (no oil) until very hot. Sear the courgette coins for 1–2 min per side until properly charred. The dry heat gives a smoky char that mirrors the haddock.
In the poaching liquid (don't discard it!), melt half the butter over low heat. Soften the garlic and lemongrass for 2–3 minutes until fragrant — don't brown.
Add the white wine and simmer to reduce by half.
Off the heat: whisk in the remaining cold butter, lemon juice, fish sauce, chilli and the zest. Season.
Fold the flaked haddock and most of the courgette into the sauce, keeping everything warm.
Plate the crispy potatoes, top with the haddock and courgette mixture, and spoon the butter sauce over everything. Scatter with herbs and a lemon wedge.

pro_tips: The dry-pan char on courgette is the whole game — wet, oily vegetables steam instead of sear. Screaming hot, no oil, short time.
The fish sauce is the secret weapon. One teaspoon tastes like 'depth' not 'fish'.
Rice instead of potatoes: steam jasmine rice (15 min) and the sauce doubles as a glaze — the lemongrass-butter over fluffy rice is very close to a lemongrass fish over rice, just milder.
